alternative: an explicit while/until/loop with reassigned locals, Kernel#loop with a break condition, or an Enumerable/Lazy pipeline; recursion only where the depth is bounded
implementation_notes: MRI offers no language-level tail-call guarantee: the only knob is the experimental :tailcall_optimization flag on RubyVM::InstructionSequence.compile_option, which is MRI-specific, off by default and documented as subject to change between versions, so user code that depends on it is depending on an implementation detail. Deep recursion therefore ends in SystemStackError. Ruby's realization of the pattern is its loop form: while/until or Kernel#loop with the accumulator reassigned in locals, Enumerable chains for collection folds, and recursion only where depth is bounded by the data.
idiom_name: explicit while/loop with reassigned locals (MRI guarantees no elimination)
pitfalls: SystemStackError arrives without a useful traceback and recovering from it in application code is not a strategy - a deep recursive traversal is a crash, not a rescueable exception.
The :tailcall_optimization option is a compile-time setting for iseqs compiled after it is set, is global to the process, and does not exist on JRuby or TruffleRuby, so it cannot back library code.
Blocks and procs do not become tail calls: recursion through yield/proc.call builds frames like any method call, which surprises Enumerable-style helpers.
